A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the inner density profiles of dark matter halos are determined primarily by the amount of specific angular momentum imparted to the halo by secondary perturbative effects, and that tidal torques play an important role in determining the specific angular momentum of the dark matter.
the density profiles in N-body simulations of dark matter halos are not cusps, but are instead flat or even cores.

the density distribution of the dark matter halos is a result of the competition between the angular momentum and the gravitational force, and it is the loss of angular momentum that leads to the cuspy central profile.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the density profiles of halos formed in N-body and semianalytically constructed simulations are remarkably similar, and the differences that do exist may not be due to the different formation mechanisms.
the specific angular momentum profile in halos is intimately related to the density profile.

the density profile of a dark matter halo is not a simple function of its mass, concentration, and formation redshift, but rather depends on the history of angular momentum imparted to the halo by tidal torques, and the history of secondary perturbations.
